Space-time interaction: Knox test and transmission chains

Source: vignettes/knox_test_en.Rmd
knox_test_en.Rmd

Dengue is transmitted by Aedes aegypti, which flies short distances, and the virus takes days (the extrinsic and intrinsic incubation periods) to pass from one person to the next. So, when there is local transmission, cases are closer in space and time than expected if space and time were independent. The Knox test (Knox 1964) counts the pairs of cases that are close in both space (less than ds metres) and time (less than dt days) and compares that number with its distribution when the dates are permuted at random (Monte Carlo). Each close pair is a space-time link, and the linked cases form the transmission chains.

The example uses sim_dengue, simulated geocoded cases of the metropolitan area of Guadalajara; with the real geocoded dataset the steps are the same.

library(denhotspots)
library(ggplot2)

1. The cases of a season

knox_test() needs a table with the coordinates (x, y) and the date of onset of symptoms (onset):

x <- subset(sim_dengue, ANO == 2024)
x <- data.frame(x = x$long, y = x$lat, onset = x$FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT)
nrow(x)
#> [1] 1680

2. Knox test

The windows are 400 m (the flight range of Ae. aegypti plus the movement of people around the house) and 20 days (the time between two cases of the same chain); the coordinates are projected (crs = "+proj=eqc", metres) and the test uses 1,000 permutations.

res <- knox_test(x = x, crs = "+proj=eqc", dt = 20, ds = 400, sym = 1000,
                 sp_link = FALSE, planar_coord = FALSE)
res$knox
#> $knox
#> [1] 3875
#> 
#> $p_value
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $RR
#> [1] 1.148744
  • knox: number of pairs of cases close in space and time (space-time links);
  • p_value: proportion of the permutations with at least as many pairs;
  • RR: ratio between the observed and the expected number of pairs.

A small p_value (and RR > 1) means space-time interaction: local transmission.

3. Map of the transmission chains

res$space_time_link has one line per link (EPSG:4326) and res$x the cases (in the projected coordinates). The map shows the links coloured by the epidemiological week of the cases, as transmission_chains_map() does in an interactive map.

cases <- sf::st_as_sf(res$x, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = "+proj=eqc")
cases <- sf::st_transform(cases, 4326)
cases$week <- cut(lubridate::epiweek(cases$onset), c(0, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 53),
                  labels = c("1-25", "26-30", "31-35", "36-40", "41-45", "46-53"))
linked <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(cases, sf::st_buffer(res$space_time_link, 1))) > 0

loc <- rgeomex::extract_locality(cve_edo = "14",
                                 locality = c("Guadalajara", "Zapopan", "Tlaquepaque", "Tonalá"))
pal <- c("#2166AC", "#1B9E77", "#A6D854", "#F2B134", "#E6550D", "#B2182B")

ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = loc, fill = "grey93", colour = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = cases[!linked, ], colour = "grey55", size = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = res$space_time_link, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_sf(data = cases[linked, ], aes(colour = week), size = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "Week") +
    theme_void()

Space-time links (400 m, 20 days) of the cases of 2024.

The linked cases (in colour) form the chains; the grey points are cases without a link. With the real data, transmission_chains_map() makes this map interactive directly from the geocoded dataset:

transmission_chains_map(geocoded_dataset = sim_dengue,
                        cve_edo = "14", locality = "Guadalajara",
                        dengue_cases = "Probable")

4. The chains by season 

by_year <- lapply(2019:2024, function(y) {
    d <- subset(sim_dengue, ANO == y)
    d <- data.frame(x = d$long, y = d$lat, onset = d$FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT)
    k <- knox_test(x = d, crs = "+proj=eqc", dt = 20, ds = 400, sym = 999,
                   sp_link = FALSE, planar_coord = FALSE)$knox
    data.frame(year = y, cases = nrow(d), links = k$knox,
               RR = round(k$RR, 2), p_value = k$p_value)
})
do.call(rbind, by_year)
#>   year cases links   RR p_value
#> 1 2019  1413  2370 1.17       0
#> 2 2020   414   318 1.40       0
#> 3 2021   259   257 1.72       0
#> 4 2022   597   624 1.33       0
#> 5 2023  1139  1665 1.27       0
#> 6 2024  1680  3875 1.15       0

References

  • Knox EG (1964). The detection of space-time interactions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C, 13(1), 25-30.
  • Tango T (2010). Statistical Methods for Disease Clustering. Springer.
